Inside Out 2.text: It was the highest-grossing animated film ever until Ne Zha 2 overtook it nine months later.
Inside Out 2.evidence: becoming the highest-grossing film by Pixar and the highest-grossing animated film of all time, though it was later overtaken by Ne Zha 2 (2025) just nine months after its initial release.

Incredibles 2.text: It lost both the Golden Globe and the Oscar for animated feature to Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse.
Incredibles 2.evidence: and was nominated for Best Animated Feature Film at the 76th Golden Globe Awards and 91st Academy Awards, but lost both to Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse.

Toy Story 5.text: Taylor Swift contributed the single "I Knew It, I Knew You".
Toy Story 5.evidence: It was the tenth Pixar film scored by Randy Newman, while Taylor Swift contributed the single "I Knew It, I Knew You".

Toy Story 4.text: Don Rickles, who died in 2017, still voices Mr. Potato Head, through unused archive audio.
Toy Story 4.evidence: Don Rickles, who died in 2017, posthumously reprises his role as Mr. Potato Head through unused archive audio.

Toy Story 3.text: The first animated film to reach $1 billion at the box office.
Toy Story 3.evidence: It was also the first animated film to reach $1 billion at the box office, and was the highest-grossing animated film until the release of Frozen in 2013

Finding Dory.text: Its Marine Life Institute is based on the crew's research trips to the Monterey Bay Aquarium.
Finding Dory.evidence: The fictional Marine Life Institute depicted extensively in the film is based on the production team's research trips to the Monterey Bay Aquarium, the Marine Mammal Center and the Vancouver Aquarium.

Finding Nemo.text: The best-selling DVD of all time, with over 40 million copies sold by 2006.
Finding Nemo.evidence: Finding Nemo is the best-selling DVD title of all time, with over 40 million copies sold as of 2006

Inside Out.text: Pete Docter came up with it after watching his daughter's personality change as she grew older.
Inside Out.evidence: Docter conceived Inside Out in October 2009 after observing changes in his daughter's personality as she grew older.

Coco.text: The first film with a nine-figure budget to have an all-Latino principal cast.
Coco.evidence: With a cost of $175–225 million, Coco is the first film with a nine-figure budget to feature an all-Latino principal cast.

Monsters University.text: Planned as a sequel, it became a prequel: Mike and Sulley's college years, before Monsters, Inc.
Monsters University.evidence: A Pixar-made sequel was confirmed in 2010 and in 2011, it was announced that the film would instead be a prequel titled Monsters University.
